questions.question: Why is extra information such as tables or graphical models added to natural‑language requirements?

options.A: To reduce the number of requirements documents needed
options.B: To illustrate how computations proceed, system state changes, user interactions, and action sequences
options.C: To replace the need for any textual description
options.D: To ensure the requirements are written in a programming language

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Adding tables or graphical models helps show the flow of computations, state changes, and user interactions, as described on page 24.

---

questions.question: Which advantage of structured specifications over pure natural language is highlighted in the text?

options.A: They eliminate the need for testing altogether
options.C: They reduce variability in the specification and organise requirements more effectively
options.D: They guarantee the system will have no bugs

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] Structured specifications reduce variability and organise requirements, as noted on page 23.

---

questions.question: Even with structured specifications, what difficulty remains when specifying complex computations such as insulin dose calculation?

options.A: Inability to represent any computation at all
options.B: Difficulty writing the requirements in a clear and unambiguous way
options.C: Lack of any graphical representation options
options.D: The requirement text becomes excessively long

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] The text states that it is still sometimes difficult to write clear, unambiguous requirements for complex computations (page 24).

---

questions.question: The tabular specification of computation shown for an insulin pump (Fig. 4.14) is most likely used to represent which kind of information?

options.A: The physical layout of the pump hardware
options.B: The step‑by‑step calculation of insulin dose
options.C: The network protocol used by the pump

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The tabular specification details the computation process, i.e., insulin dose calculation (page 24).

questions.question: In the requirement description format, the “description of the side effects (if any) of the operation” serves to document what?

options.A: The primary functional behavior of the operation
options.C: Potential additional effects that occur when the operation is executed
options.D: The hardware resources needed for the operation

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] Page 23 lists a side‑effects description as a distinct element of a requirement.

questions.question: How can structured language notations highlight key elements of a requirement?

options.B: By applying shading or different fonts
options.C: By writing the text in a different language

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Easy] The text mentions that shading or different fonts can be used to highlight key elements (page 23).

questions.question: The citation of Dijkstra’s “The Humble Programmer” (page 36) is most likely included to support which point in the discussion?

options.A: The historical development of programming languages
options.B: The need for disciplined, structured approaches to specification
options.C: The importance of humility in software project management
options.D: The evolution of computer hardware design

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Dijkstra’s work is frequently invoked to argue for disciplined, structured methods, aligning with the text’s emphasis on structured specifications (page 36).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage as a way to add extra information to natural‑language requirements?
questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The passage lists tables, graphical models, and programming‑language constructs, but does not mention flowcharts (pages 24 & 23).

questions.question: The structured specification illustrated in Figure 4.13 primarily aims to improve which aspect of requirements?

options.B: Clarity and unambiguity of the specification
options.C: Execution speed of the final system

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Figure 4.13 is presented as a means to make requirements clearer and more unambiguous (page 24).

questions.question: In structured language notations, templates are primarily used to specify what?

options.A: System requirements in a uniform format

questions.explanation: [Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] Templates provide a uniform way to specify system requirements, as described on page 23.
